profile.name: Junghun Chae
profile.introduction: I study complex biological systems through quantitative modeling and data analysis, with work spanning enzyme kinetics, circadian dynamics, microbiome metabolism, and collective behavior.
profile.currentFocusDetail: Current projects include metabolic-network reconstruction for Segatella Copri and game theory in the Vicsek model.

research.title: Biochemical dynamics
research.summary: Developing and studying rate laws beyond standard steady-state assumptions, including relaxation dynamics and time-varying molecular concentrations.

research.title: Microbiome & metabolism
research.summary: Modeling metabolic networks and microbial communities through network reconstruction and dynamic flux balance analysis.

research.title: Collective & information dynamics
research.summary: Using multi-agent simulation, game theory, and large-scale scientific data to study collective behavior and innovation.

chunks.title: Research overview
chunks.text: Junghun Chae is a physics M.S.–Ph.D. student at Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology (UNIST). His CV documents research in biochemical kinetics, circadian dynamics, microbiome and metabolic-network modeling, collective-agent dynamics, biological information processing, and large-scale bibliometric analysis.

chunks.title: Graduate education
chunks.text: Junghun Chae has been enrolled in an M.S.–Ph.D. program in Physics at Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology (UNIST), Korea, since March 2021. The CV lists the program as continuing to the present.

chunks.title: Undergraduate education
chunks.text: Junghun Chae earned a Bachelor of Science in Physics with a minor in Computer Science from Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology (UNIST), Korea, from March 2017 to February 2021.

chunks.title: Relaxation dynamics in Michaelis–Menten kinetics
chunks.text: Chae, J.; Lim, R.; Martin, T. L. P.; Ghim, C.-M.; and Kim, P.-J. published “Enlightening the blind spot of the Michaelis–Menten rate law: The role of relaxation dynamics in molecular complex formation” in Journal of Theoretical Biology, volume 597, article 111989, in 2025. The CV marks Chae, Lim, and Martin as co-first authors.

chunks.title: Generalized Michaelis–Menten rate law
chunks.text: Lim, R.; Martin, T. L. P.; Chae, J.; Kim, W.; Ghim, C.-M.; and Kim, P.-J. published “Generalized Michaelis–Menten Rate Law with time-varying molecular concentrations” in PLOS Computational Biology 19(12), e1011711, in 2023. The CV marks Lim, Martin, and Chae as co-first authors.

chunks.title: Backward simulation protocol
chunks.text: Chae, J.; Lim, R.; Ghim, C.-M.; and Kim, P.-J. published “Backward simulation for inferring hidden biomolecular kinetic profiles” in STAR Protocols 2(4), 100958, in 2021. The CV marks Chae and Lim as co-first authors.

chunks.title: Cost-effective circadian mechanism
chunks.text: Lim, R.; Chae, J.; Somers, D. E.; Ghim, C.-M.; and Kim, P.-J. published “Cost-effective circadian mechanism: rhythmic degradation of circadian proteins spontaneously emerges without rhythmic post-translational regulation” in iScience 24, 102726, in 2021. The CV marks Lim and Chae as co-first authors.

chunks.title: Warning signals for innovative genetic research
chunks.text: A manuscript titled “Warning signals for the long-term innovative potential of genetic research based on 20 million papers and patents” is listed in the CV as under review. The listed authors begin with J. Chae, W. Kim, W. Jung, D. Jeong, R. Lim, M. Chamlagain, and G. Jung, followed by additional authors. The CV marks Chae, Kim, Jung, Jeong, and Lim as co-first authors. It must not be described as a published paper.

chunks.title: Metabolic network reconstruction of Segatella Copri
chunks.text: The CV lists “High-profile reconstruction of metabolic network of Segatella Copri” as an ongoing project beginning in 2025. The advisors are Cheol-Min Ghim at UNIST and Pan-Jun Kim at Hong Kong Baptist University. No project result is stated in the CV.

chunks.title: Game theory in the Vicsek model
chunks.text: The CV lists a 2025 project on game theory in the Vicsek model, advised by Cheol-Min Ghim at UNIST. Related 2025 presentations covered multilevel selection in mobile agents and how initial configurations change their dynamics. The CV also lists 2025 technical experience in multi-agent simulation with GPU and CUDA.

chunks.title: Information processing in biological systems
chunks.text: The CV lists a 2024 project titled “Information processing in biological systems,” advised by Cheol-Min Ghim at UNIST. The CV does not provide further methods or results for this project.

chunks.title: Bibliometric analysis of genetic research
chunks.text: From 2023 to 2024, Junghun Chae worked on a gene bibliometric review of papers and patents, advised by Cheol-Min Ghim at UNIST and Pan-Jun Kim at Hong Kong Baptist University. The CV lists technical experience in big-data analysis using PubMed and PATSTAT data in 2024 and a related manuscript based on 20 million papers and patents that is under review.

chunks.title: Michaelis–Menten kinetics and relaxation dynamics
chunks.text: From 2022 to 2024, Junghun Chae worked on Michaelis–Menten kinetics for circadian proteins, advised by Cheol-Min Ghim at UNIST and Pan-Jun Kim at Hong Kong Baptist University. Related publications examine time-varying molecular concentrations and the role of relaxation dynamics beyond standard Michaelis–Menten assumptions. Conference presentations from 2022 to 2024 addressed rate laws beyond steady-state or adiabatic approximations and applications to circadian dynamics and biological feedback control.

chunks.title: Dynamic flux balance analysis of the gut microbiome
chunks.text: The CV lists a 2021 project applying dynamic flux balance analysis to the mammalian gut microbiome, advised by Cheol-Min Ghim at UNIST and Pan-Jun Kim at Hong Kong Baptist University. A 2025 Korean Physical Society presentation was titled “Microbiome Dynamics under Dietary Shifts.” The CV does not state a publication from this project.

chunks.title: Rhythmic degradation of circadian proteins
chunks.text: The CV lists a 2020 project on rhythmic degradation of circadian proteins, advised by Cheol-Min Ghim at UNIST and Pan-Jun Kim at Hong Kong Baptist University. A 2021 iScience paper reports a cost-effective circadian mechanism in which rhythmic degradation emerges without rhythmic post-translational regulation. Conference presentations in 2022 addressed cost-efficient circadian rhythms and rhythmic protein degradation.

chunks.title: Computational and mathematical methods
chunks.text: The CV lists technical experience in GPU-based multi-agent simulation with CUDA (2025), high-precision diagonalization of matrices of size 10,000 or larger (2024), reinforcement learning and deep learning (2022), the Gillespie algorithm and linear noise approximation (2022), linear programming (2021), and numerical ordinary differential equations (2020).

chunks.title: Programming, software, and languages
chunks.text: The CV lists Python experience with NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, Pandas, and FEniCS; C and C++ experience including CUDA C++ and libTorch; and software experience with Linux, Git, and Inkscape. Bioinformatics software listed includes Metaphlan, Kraken, and QIIME. Other tools include LaTeX and Nsight System. Language proficiency is listed as Korean native, English proficient, and Japanese proficient.

chunks.title: Teaching experience
chunks.text: At UNIST, Junghun Chae served as a teaching assistant for Network Science in Fall 2025, Classical Mechanics II in Fall 2022, Classical Mechanics I in Spring 2022, Network Science for Complex Systems in Fall 2021, and History of Science and Technology in Spring 2019.

chunks.title: Other academic experience
chunks.text: The CV lists a Research Assistant position at Hong Kong Baptist University from April to September 2021. It also lists peer-review experience for Scientific Reports in Winter 2021 and curriculum development for Network Science and Machine Intelligence in the UNIST Department of Physics in Fall 2021.

chunks.title: Conference presentations, 2024–2025
chunks.text: The CV lists these recent presentations: “Game Theory in Mobile Agents - Introduction of multilevel selection” at the Korean Physical Society in October 2025; “Game Theory in Mobile Agents - How initial configuration changes dynamics” at the 23rd Workshop for Statistical Physics in August 2025; “Microbiome Dynamics under Dietary Shifts” at the Korean Physical Society in April 2025; “A Scientometric Study on the Innovative Frontiers in Genetic Research” at the Korean Physical Society in October 2024; and “Improving the blind spot of the Michaelis–Menten rate law” at the Korean Physical Society in April 2024.

chunks.title: Conference presentations, 2022–2023
chunks.text: The CV lists these presentations: “Generalized Michaelis-Menten Rate Law with Time-varying Molecular Concentrations” at ICBP 2023; “Effective rate law for biological feedback control” at the Korean Physical Society in April 2023; “Michaelis–Menten Rate Law beyond Adiabatic Approximations” at Winter Q-Bio in February 2023; “Rhythmic protein degradation for cost-effective circadian oscillation” at ICSB 2022; “The Michaelis–Menten Rate Law beyond the Steady State and Its Application to Circadian Dynamics” at the Korean Physical Society in April 2022; and “Post-translational modification for cost-efficient circadian rhythms” at the Biophysical Society Annual Meetings in February 2022.
